symptom: `fmt --upgrade --header` refused the header over `$R = min($Years.Yr)` (and `max(`, `avg(`, and `set $R = min(…)`) with MDL-V1-LIST "the operand is not a variable (a nested call or an expression)", although mdl 0 builds one Aggregate list activity from it and describe writes it back as `minimum`; under mdl 1 the short form is a syntax error, so the script could not take the header.
cause: min/max/avg are not listAggregateOperation keywords: the call parses as the OQL aggregateFunction rule, which buildAggregateFunctionAsCall maps to MINIMUM/MAXIMUM/AVERAGE for the flow builder. setCallFix finds the call through singleListCall, which knew only ListOperationContext and ListAggregateOperationContext, so the AggregateFunctionContext looked like an arbitrary expression and got the nested-call reason.
fix: singleListCall also returns an AggregateFunctionContext, and callFormFix dispatches it to aggregateFunctionFix, which mirrors buildSetAggregate's reading of the operand: `$L.Attr` / `$L/Attr` -> `minimum|maximum|average|sum $L by Attr`, a bare list only for count; `*`, `distinct`, a bare list for the others and a non-plain attribute keep a reason.
insight: A rewrite finds its construct by parse-tree shape, but the gate that records it keys on the AST, which normalises several grammar rules into one FunctionCallExpr; every rule that normalises into the gated AST needs a matching case in the fix. Enumerate them from the AST builder (buildAggregateFunctionAsCall, buildListAggregateAsFunction, buildListOperationAsFunction), not from the grammar rule the canonical spelling uses. A sweep of every list/aggregate short form, with and without `set`, under --header found min/max/avg as the only gap.
test: mdl/upgrade/gated_test.go TestUpgrade_GatedRewrites (min/MAX/avg/set min), TestUpgrade_UnrewritableBlocksTheHeader (min over a bare list, count(*))
